verdict.rationale: GitHub's own marketing copy describes updating vulnerable dependencies, reducing application vulnerabilities with security campaigns and Copilot Autofix, and detecting leaked secrets. These imply first-party dependency and code-security capabilities. However, the evidence never says that repositories are automatically scanned, and it gives no detail on how detection works. missing for 10: explicit documentation of automatic dependency vulnerability scanning and code scanning (triggers, coverage, alerts), in-depth first-party docs beyond marketing taglines, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have my repository automatically scanned for vulnerable dependencies and code security issues

citations.quote: Update vulnerable dependencies with supported fixes for breaking changes.
Leverage security campaigns and Copilot Autofix to reduce application vulnerabilities.
Detect, prevent, and remediate leaked secrets across your organization.
GitHub push protection confirms and displays an active secret, and blocks the push.
